mapa.titulo: Where Salta is growing, and why
mapa.intro: Six territories, and what is happening in each.
mapa.rotulo_quien: Profile and opportunities of the area

territorios.bajada: Where heritage begins to change hands
territorios.cambia: The centre stopped growing outwards and grew by transformation. Companies, studios and offices now sit next to cafés and shops, and the colonial houses have left the traditional residential market.
territorios.quien: Companies, professional practices, entrepreneurs, tourism and people who want urban, connected living.

territorios.cambia: One of the main expansion corridors in Salta. Every new development consolidates a residential ecosystem that keeps growing.
territorios.quien: Young families, professionals and anyone planning a long-term home without giving up the city.

territorios.bajada: Two territories, two ways of living
territorios.cambia: San Lorenzo Viejo is a consolidated market with a stable setting. San Lorenzo Chico is no longer only residential: schools, offices, gyms and restaurants let people live and work in the same place.
territorios.quien: Established families in Viejo. In Chico, young families, professionals and entrepreneurs who blend home, work and quality of life.

territorios.cambia: The expansion southwards finds its engine here. Being close to the airport and the main access roads sustains steady demand, alongside new neighbourhoods, services and shops.
territorios.quien: Working families, professionals and people tied to commerce and logistics who value access.

territorios.bajada: Investing is also choosing a way to live
territorios.cambia: The Calchaquí Valleys are a different market: the purchase decision mixes heritage, enjoyment and yield. Demand for second homes and tourism-linked investment keeps growing.
territorios.quien: People looking for a second home, heritage investors, tourism entrepreneurs and families who put experience and nature first.

territorios.cambia: Vaqueros is emerging as an eco-cultural answer, more bohemian and open, with a strong sense of community. The new urban and environmental planning code and the widened access road reinforce the area.
territorios.quien: Couples aged 30 to 45 who work downtown or remotely and want their children to grow up close to nature. Artists, architects and designers. Short-stay rental investors.
